songs.title: What Are We Fighting For?
songs.attribution: "What Are We Fighting For?" by A Beautiful Tomorrow, from the album "What Are We Fighting For?". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 262816); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Fool In Modern Times
songs.attribution: "Fool In Modern Times" by A Jovian Night, from the album "A Jovian Night - 03 - Fool In Modern Times". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 233060); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: A la nanita nana
songs.artist: José Ramón Gomis / Juan Francisco Muñoz y Pabón
songs.attribution: Published in Madrid in 1904 as "La nana, balada al Niño Jesús", music by José Ramón Gomis (died 1939), words by Juan Francisco Muñoz y Pabón (died 1920); sung here in the form that passed into Spanish oral tradition as a carol and lullaby. Both authors died more than 80 years ago, so melody and words are public domain. The middle section turns to D major, so its F sharps, C sharps and B naturals are expected to show as out-of-key.

songs.title: Abide with Me
songs.artist: William Henry Monk / Henry Francis Lyte
songs.attribution: Words by Henry Francis Lyte (1847; he died that year), sung to the tune "Eventide" written by William Henry Monk for Hymns Ancient and Modern (1861; he died in 1889). Melody and words are public domain worldwide. The F sharp on "abide" (end of the second line) is a chromatic note of the original tune and is expected to show as out-of-key.

songs.title: take a seat
songs.attribution: "take a seat" by Abrids, from the album "Fashion Reptile". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 109838); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: le manoir
songs.attribution: "le manoir" by Adragante, from the album "un Barde". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 128293); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: After the Ball
songs.attribution: Words and music by Charles K. Harris (died 1930); published by Charles K. Harris & Co., Milwaukee, in 1892 and sung in "A Trip to Chinatown", it became the first Tin Pan Alley song to sell millions of copies. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: ASK GOD
songs.attribution: "ASK GOD" by AGORA-OU-NUNCA, from the album "ASK GOD". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 276468); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Ain't We Got Fun
songs.artist: Richard A. Whiting / Gus Kahn and Raymond B. Egan
songs.attribution: Music by Richard A. Whiting (died 1938), words by Gus Kahn (died 1941) and Raymond B. Egan (died 1952); published by Jerome H. Remick & Co. in 1921. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Akatonbo
songs.attribution: "Red Dragonfly": music by Kōsaku Yamada (died 1965), set in 1927 to a poem by Rofū Miki (died 1964) written in 1921. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada). Melody and all four verses from the score and numbered notation in Yamada's own songbook (National Diet Library digital collection).

songs.title: Quiet haven
songs.attribution: "Quiet haven" by Al Ryden, from the album "ROCK hovering over the abyss". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 149239); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: alobi e menestrello
songs.attribution: "alobi e menestrello" by Alobi, from the album "Alobi e Menestrello". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 139914); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Aloha ʻOe
songs.attribution: Words and music by Liliʻuokalani (1838-1917), written in 1878 and published with an 1884 copyright; public domain. Melody and word underlay follow the original sheet music, where some two-syllable words (pali, nihi, hele, liko, uka) are printed under a single note; the chorus keeps her two English lines. The passing G# shows as out-of-key.

songs.title: Alouette
songs.attribution: French-Canadian traditional children's song, first printed in A Pocket Song Book for the Use of Students and Graduates of McGill College (Montreal, 1879); anonymous, public domain.

songs.title: Am I Blue?
songs.attribution: Music by Harry Akst (died 1963), words by Grant Clarke (died 1931); introduced by Ethel Waters in the film "On with the Show!" and published by M. Witmark & Sons in 1929. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Amazing Grace
songs.attribution: Words by John Newton (Olney Hymns, 1779); the tune "New Britain" is an American folk melody first printed in 1829 and joined to Newton's text in William Walker's Southern Harmony (1835), so both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Зая, еду к тебе...
songs.attribution: "Зая, еду к тебе..." by Anastasia Glam, from the album "Зая, еду к тебе...". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 282450); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Angels We Have Heard on High
songs.attribution: The melody "Gloria" is that of the anonymous traditional French carol "Les anges dans nos campagnes" (first printed in 1842); the English words were written in 1862 by James Chadwick (he died in 1882). Melody and words are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: April Showers
songs.attribution: Music by Louis Silvers (died 1954), words by B. G. "Buddy" DeSylva (died 1950); introduced by Al Jolson in "Bombo" and published by Jerome H. Remick & Co. in 1921. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Arirang
songs.attribution: Traditional Korean folk song (the "Bonjo Arirang" of Gyeonggi), transcribed by Homer Hulbert in 1896; melody and words are anonymous and public domain. Written in 9/8 with the eighth note as the beat (dotted quarter = 3 beats), so the tempo is in eighths (about 50 dotted quarters per minute).

songs.title: Arroz con leche
songs.attribution: Anonymous traditional singing game from Spain, recorded in Spanish folk-song collections of the 19th century and sung throughout Latin America ever since; melody and words have no known author and are public domain. This is the widespread Latin American text ("de San Nicolás"). Melody checked against the scores and MIDI at Mama Lisa's World.

songs.title: Au clair de la lune
songs.attribution: French traditional children's song, melody and words from the 18th century (the words are sometimes attributed to Lully, 17th century); anonymous, public domain.

songs.title: Auld Lang Syne
songs.attribution: Words by Robert Burns (1788), sung to the traditional Scots tune first paired with the text in George Thomson's Select Songs of Scotland (1799); both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Aura Lee
songs.attribution: Music by George R. Poulton (1828-1867), words by W. W. Fosdick (1825-1862), published in Cincinnati in 1861 (the tune later used for "Love Me Tender"); public domain.

songs.title: Avalon
songs.artist: Vincent Rose / Al Jolson and B. G. DeSylva
songs.attribution: Music by Vincent Rose (died 1944), words by Al Jolson (died 1950) and B. G. DeSylva (died 1950); published by Jerome H. Remick & Co. in 1920. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Ballin' the Jack
songs.attribution: Music by Chris Smith (died 1949), words by Jim Burris (died 1923); published by Jos. W. Stern & Co. in 1913. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Be Thou My Vision
songs.attribution: The tune "Slane" is a traditional Irish air first printed in Patrick W. Joyce's Old Irish Folk Music and Songs (1909). The words are Eleanor Hull's 1912 verse setting (she died in 1935) of Mary Byrne's 1905 translation (she died in 1931) of an early Irish poem. Melody and words are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Beautiful Dreamer
songs.attribution: Words and music by Stephen C. Foster (1826-1864), published posthumously by Wm. A. Pond & Co., New York, in 1864; public domain. Written in 9/8 with the eighth note as the beat (dotted quarter = 3 beats), so the tempo is in eighths (about 63 dotted quarters per minute). The C# is Foster's chromatic lower neighbour.

songs.title: Bella Ciao
songs.attribution: Italian folk melody (older than the words, related to a 19th-century mondina work song); the partisan words are anonymous, from the 1940s, first published in 1953 (Canti della Resistenza italiana). Anonymous and traditional, public domain.

songs.title: Caught on the Wire
songs.attribution: "Caught on the Wire" by Berkley Mallin, from the album "Caught on the Wire". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 291627); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Tool and Die
songs.attribution: "Tool and Die" by BETP5, from the album "Arrow Songs". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 158541); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Bill Bailey, Won't You Please Come Home
songs.attribution: Words and music by Hughie Cannon (died 1912); published by Howley, Haviland & Dresser, New York, in 1902. The chorus words are those of the 1902 edition, with the dialect spellings written in standard English. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Oh My Love
songs.attribution: "Oh My Love" by Billie, from the album "Oh My Love". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 213772); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Не подходи ко мне
songs.attribution: "Не подходи ко мне" by Black_Angel, from the album "Ne podhodi ko mne!". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 182498); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Blow the Man Down
songs.attribution: Anonymous halyard shanty of the Atlantic packet ships, quoted in print by 1867 and published in L. A. Smith's The Music of the Waters (1888); the words here are stanzas 1 and 4 of R. R. Terry's The Shanty Book (1921). Traditional melody and words, public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Brahms' Lullaby (Wiegenlied)
songs.attribution: Melody: "Wiegenlied" Op. 49 No. 4 by Johannes Brahms (1868); the English words "Lullaby and good night" are the traditional 19th-century translation. Both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: By the Light of the Silvery Moon
songs.attribution: Music by Gus Edwards (died 1945), words by Edward Madden (died 1952); published by Gus Edwards Music Publishing Co., New York, in 1909 and sung in the Ziegfeld Follies of 1909. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Bye Bye Blackbird
songs.attribution: Music by Ray Henderson (died 1970), words by Mort Dixon (died 1956); published by Jerome H. Remick & Co. in 1926. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Careless Love
songs.attribution: Traditional American blues ballad, sung in New Orleans and the South by the 1900s; melody and words are stanzas 1 and 2 as printed in Carl Sandburg's The American Songbag (1927) from R. W. Gordon's collection. Public domain: traditional, published before 1931 (United States) and no individual author (Canada).

songs.title: Carolina in the Morning
songs.attribution: Music by Walter Donaldson (died 1947), words by Gus Kahn (died 1941); published by Jerome H. Remick & Co. in 1922. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Charleston
songs.attribution: Music by James P. Johnson (died 1955), words by Cecil Mack (died 1944); introduced in the revue "Runnin' Wild" and published by Harms, Inc. in 1923. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Cielito Lindo
songs.attribution: Mexican canción by Quirino Mendoza y Cortés (died 1957), published in 1882; the verses adapt older Spanish coplas. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Ciranda, cirandinha
songs.attribution: Anonymous Brazilian circle-game song of Portuguese origin; the verses are old folk quatrains found in 19th-century collections and the tune was already in print when Heitor Villa-Lobos quoted it in "O Polichinelo" (1918), so melody and words are public domain. Melody checked against the score and MIDI at Mama Lisa's World (transposed from B flat to G); each half is sung twice, as in that score.

songs.title: Feel (Stripped)
songs.attribution: "Feel (Stripped)" by Cortez, licensed CC BY 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/1481500/feel-stripped); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: Daisy Bell (A Bicycle Built for Two)
songs.attribution: Words and music by Harry Dacre (Frank Dean, died 1922); published in 1892 and made famous in the music halls and on Tin Pan Alley. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: When diamonds turn to dust
songs.attribution: "When diamonds turn to dust" by Dan Falvey, from the album "When diamonds turn to dust". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 282418); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Danny Boy
songs.attribution: The melody is the traditional Irish "Londonderry Air" (first printed by George Petrie in 1855); the words were written by Frederic Weatherly in 1913 (he died in 1929), so both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Eternity
songs.attribution: "Eternity" by David Crowe, from the album "Eternity". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 338461); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: De colores
songs.attribution: Anonymous traditional song of Spain and Mexico; the melody came from Spain in the colonial era and the song has circulated in the Americas for centuries, with no known author. Only the old first verse and refrain are used (not the 20th-century added verses), so melody and words are public domain. The B flat on "lucir" is a chromatic passing note and is expected to show as out-of-key.

songs.title: Voglio ballare
songs.attribution: "Voglio ballare" by De Vito Tatiana, from the album "Voglio ballare". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 230819); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Deck the Halls
songs.attribution: Melody: the 16th-century Welsh New Year's tune "Nos Galan"; English words by Thomas Oliphant (1862). Both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Outta Here
songs.attribution: "Outta Here" by Devon Elizabeth, from the album "The Vault". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 151894); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Die Gedanken sind frei
songs.attribution: German folk song; the words circulated on broadsheets around 1780, the melody dates from about 1810-1820 and both were printed together in Hoffmann von Fallersleben and Ernst Richter's "Schlesische Volkslieder" (1842). Anonymous and public domain. Two verses.

songs.title: Dinah
songs.artist: Harry Akst / Sam M. Lewis and Joe Young
songs.attribution: Music by Harry Akst (died 1963), words by Sam M. Lewis (died 1959) and Joe Young (died 1939); published by Henry Waterson, Inc. in 1925 and introduced by Ethel Waters. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Don't Forget To Breathe
songs.attribution: "Don't Forget To Breathe" by Dirty Dukes, from the album "Don't Forget To Breathe". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 155331); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: ¿Dónde vas, Alfonso XII?
songs.attribution: Anonymous Spanish ballad sung by children in Madrid after the death of Queen Mercedes in 1878, a reworking of a much older romance ("¿Dónde vas, el caballero?"); it has no known author and has been in oral tradition since the 19th century, so melody and words are public domain. Melody checked against the score on Wikimedia Commons.

songs.title: Down by the Old Mill Stream
songs.attribution: Words and music by Tell Taylor (died 1937); first published in 1910 (Star Music, Chicago, then M. Witmark & Sons). Earl K. Smith (died 1954), who later claimed a share of the music, also died before 1972. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Down by the Riverside
songs.attribution: African-American spiritual, sung since before the Civil War and first published in Plantation Melodies (1918); anonymous, public domain. The A# is the traditional chromatic lower neighbour in "down by the riverside".

songs.title: Drunken Sailor
songs.attribution: Anonymous capstan shanty sung on British and American ships since at least the 1830s (first described in an account of an 1839 whaling voyage); words as printed in R. R. Terry's The Shanty Book (1921). Traditional melody and words, public domain worldwide. The tune is in the Dorian mode, so the B natural on "drunken sailor" (third line) is expected to show as out-of-key.

songs.title: Du gamla, du fria
songs.attribution: Words written in 1844 by Richard Dybeck (1811-1877) to a traditional folk-ballad tune from Västmanland; sung as Sweden's national anthem. Melody and words are public domain. The last line is repeated.

songs.title: Freifliegen
songs.attribution: "Freifliegen" by Durch Dick und Dünn, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/34276/freifliegen/lyrics); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: Time flies
songs.attribution: "Time flies" by Ehma, from the album "Time flies". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 611147); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Ekla Chalo Re
songs.attribution: Words and music by Rabindranath Tagore, written in 1905 to a Baul-style tune (Tagore died in 1941), so both are public domain. This is the refrain ("If no one answers your call, walk alone"), from the staff notation in the Sangeet Natak Akademi anthology of Tagore songs. The flat 7th (B flat) on "ekla cholo" is expected to show as out-of-key.

songs.title: Just Be
songs.attribution: "Just Be" by Ellis band, from the album "Just Be". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 143629); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Heartless
songs.attribution: "Heartless" by Evergreen Machine, from the album "Homefront". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 141952); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Five Foot Two, Eyes of Blue
songs.artist: Ray Henderson / Sam M. Lewis and Joe Young
songs.attribution: Music by Ray Henderson (died 1970), words by Sam M. Lewis (died 1959) and Joe Young (died 1939); published as "Five Foot Two, Eyes of Blue (Has Anybody Seen My Girl?)" by Leo Feist, Inc. in 1925. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: l'abandon
songs.attribution: "l'abandon" by FLO, licensed CC BY 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/48843/l-abandon/lyrics); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: For He's a Jolly Good Fellow
songs.attribution: Melody: the French song "Marlbrough s'en va-t-en guerre" (18th century); the English congratulatory words are 19th-century traditional. Both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Frankie and Johnny
songs.attribution: Traditional American murder ballad, sung from the 1890s and in print by 1912; the words are stanzas 1, 6 and 7 as collected in Carl Sandburg's The American Songbag (1927). Public domain: traditional, published before 1931 (United States) and no individual author (Canada).

songs.title: Baby Baby
songs.attribution: "Baby Baby" by Franky Barbano, from the album "The Idiot". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 185553); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Frère Jacques
songs.attribution: Traditional French nursery round, words and melody in print by the late 18th century; public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Funiculì, Funiculà
songs.attribution: Music by Luigi Denza (1846-1922), Neapolitan words by Peppino Turco (1846-1903), written in 1880 for the opening of the Vesuvius funicular; both authors died more than 70 years ago, public domain. Written in 6/8 with the eighth note as the beat (dotted quarter = 3 beats), so the tempo is in eighths (about 100 dotted quarters per minute).

songs.title: Furusato
songs.attribution: "My Old Country Home", a Ministry of Education school song published in 1914 (Jinjō shōgaku shōka, sixth grade); music by Teiichi Okano (died 1941), words by Tatsuyuki Takano (died 1947). Both are public domain.

songs.title: Poucet
songs.attribution: "Poucet" by Gamssy Ghoulz, from the album "Les chansons retrouvees". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 171597); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: The fool with a thousand ridiculous faces
songs.attribution: "The fool with a thousand ridiculous faces" by Giocol, from the album "The fool with a thousand ridiculous faces". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 409073); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Give My Regards to Broadway
songs.attribution: Words and music by George M. Cohan (died 1942), written for his musical "Little Johnny Jones" and published by F. A. Mills, New York, in 1904. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Go Down, Moses
songs.attribution: African-American spiritual from the time of slavery, first printed as sheet music in 1861-62 ("Oh! Let My People Go") and in the Fisk Jubilee Singers' Jubilee Songs (1872), whose first verse and refrain are used here. Anonymous and traditional, public domain worldwide. The D sharp on "people" is the raised leading note of the minor key and is expected to show as out-of-key.

songs.title: Go Tell It on the Mountain
songs.attribution: African-American spiritual from oral tradition, first printed in the 1900s (Folk Songs of the American Negro, 1907; Religious Folk Songs of the Negro, 1909); the Christmas verse "While shepherds kept their watching" is by John Wesley Work Jr., who died in 1925. Melody and words are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Good King Wenceslas
songs.attribution: Melody: the 13th-century spring carol "Tempus adest floridum" (printed in Piae Cantiones, 1582); words by John Mason Neale (1853). Both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Greensleeves
songs.attribution: Traditional English tune and words, registered at the Stationers' Company in 1580 and printed in A Handful of Pleasant Delights (1584); public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Hamabe no Uta
songs.attribution: "Song of the Seashore": music by Tamezō Narita (died 1945), composed by 1916 to a poem by Kokei Hayashi (died 1947) first printed in 1913, published by Senō Gakufu in 1918. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada). Verses 1 and 2 (the third verse, which Hayashi disowned, is left out), in the original key of A flat.

songs.title: Happy Birthday to You
songs.attribution: Melody by Mildred J. Hill and Patty S. Hill ("Good Morning to All", 1893); the birthday words are traditional. A 2016 US court ruling confirmed the song is in the public domain.

songs.title: Hark! The Herald Angels Sing
songs.attribution: Words by Charles Wesley (1739; he died in 1788) as altered by George Whitefield (1753; he died in 1770), sung to a melody from Felix Mendelssohn's Festgesang (1840; he died in 1847) adapted by William H. Cummings in 1855 (he died in 1915). Melody and words are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Hatikvah (The Hope)
songs.attribution: Words from Naftali Herz Imber's poem "Tikvatenu" (written 1878, printed 1886; Imber died in 1909), with the refrain in the form it had taken among the early settlers by 1905 (usually credited to Yehuda Leib Matmon-Cohen, died 1939). The melody was fitted to it in 1888 by Samuel Cohen (died 1940) from the Moldavian folk tune "Carul cu boi". All public domain.

songs.title: Haul Away, Joe
songs.attribution: Anonymous 19th-century short-haul shanty, printed in Cecil Sharp's English Folk-Chanteys (1914) and in R. R. Terry's The Shanty Book (1921), which has both the "little boy" verse and the "haul for better weather" line used here. Traditional melody and words, public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Hava Nagila
songs.attribution: Melody: a Hasidic nigun (Sadigura, 19th century), arranged by Abraham Zvi Idelsohn (died 1938), who also wrote the words in 1918 (published in Sefer Hashirim, 1922). Public domain. The raised 7th (F#) of the Jewish "Ahava Rabbah" mode is expected to show as out-of-key.

songs.title: Die Geburt
songs.attribution: "Die Geburt" by Heiko Sunfyah, from the album "Rä Wo Lu Zion". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 156347); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: He's Got the Whole World in His Hands
songs.attribution: Anonymous African-American spiritual, first published in the hymnal Spirituals Triumphant, Old and New (1927) and collected from oral tradition in the 1930s; no known author, melody and words are public domain. Only the traditional first verse is used (sung twice).

songs.title: Hevenu Shalom Aleichem
songs.attribution: Anonymous Hasidic melody (in circulation in Europe by about 1920, when Franz Xaver Haberl quoted it in a printed march); the only words are the traditional Hebrew greeting "We brought peace upon you". No known author, public domain. Sung three times through, as is usual.

songs.title: Hine E Hine
songs.attribution: Māori lullaby with words and music by Fanny Rose Howie, known as Princess Te Rangi Pai (1868-1916), written about 1907 and published in London as "A Maori Slumber Song"; public domain.

songs.title: Home on the Range
songs.attribution: Words by Dr. Brewster Higley (1872, as "My Western Home") and tune by Daniel E. Kelley (1873), first printed in the Smith County Pioneer, Kansas, in 1873; public domain worldwide.

songs.title: House of the Rising Sun
songs.attribution: Traditional American folk ballad from Appalachia, first recorded by Clarence Ashley in 1933 and sung by Georgia Turner to Alan Lomax in 1937; this is the plain traditional tune and the traditional words, not any later commercial arrangement, so both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: CHRISTMAS AVEC TOI
songs.attribution: "CHRISTMAS AVEC TOI" by I'M FRESH! YOU'RE PRETTY!, licensed CC BY 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/1173749/christmas-avec-toi/lyrics); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: I Want a Girl (Just Like the Girl That Married Dear Old Dad)
songs.attribution: Music by Harry Von Tilzer (died 1946), words by William Dillon (died 1966); published by the Harry Von Tilzer Music Publishing Co. in 1911. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: I'll See You in My Dreams
songs.attribution: Music by Isham Jones (died 1956), words by Gus Kahn (died 1941); published by Leo Feist, Inc. in 1924. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: I'm Looking Over a Four Leaf Clover
songs.attribution: Music by Harry Woods (died 1970), words by Mort Dixon (died 1956); published by Jerome H. Remick & Co. in 1927. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: In the Good Old Summer Time
songs.attribution: Music by George "Honey Boy" Evans (died 1915), words by Ren Shields (died 1913); published in 1902 and introduced by Blanche Ring. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: It Had to Be You
songs.attribution: Music by Isham Jones (died 1956), words by Gus Kahn (died 1941); published by Jerome H. Remick & Co. in 1924. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: It's a Long Way to Tipperary
songs.attribution: Words and music credited to Jack Judge (died 1938) and Harry Williams (died 1924); published by B. Feldman & Co., London, in 1912. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Ja-Da
songs.attribution: Words and music by Bob Carleton (died 1956); published by Leo Feist, Inc. in 1918. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Tu m'oublies
songs.attribution: "Tu m'oublies" by jacky.daniel, from the album "En quelques mots". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 144713); downloaded from the Internet Archive.

songs.title: Yes i love you

songs.title: Jingle Bells

The last two lines are repeated, as is usual.

songs.title: La Cucaracha

songs.title: La Golondrina
songs.attribution: Written in 1862 by the Mexican physician and composer Narciso Serradell Sevilla (1843-1910); the Spanish words are attributed to Niceto de Zamacois (died 1885), after an older poem. Both died well over 100 years ago, so melody and words are public domain. Melody checked against the voice part of the free 8notes score and MIDI (transposed from E flat to C); the F sharps are chromatic neighbour notes expected to show as out-of-key. Notes written (0.333333333) are triplet eighths.

songs.title: La Paloma
songs.attribution: Habanera written about 1860 by the Basque composer Sebastián Iradier (Yradier, died 1865) after a visit to Cuba; he wrote both the melody and the Spanish words, so the song is public domain worldwide. Melody checked against the 1906 Century Music voice-and-piano edition; the triplets against the habanera beat are original, and the single F sharp ("que sí") is a chromatic neighbour note expected to show as out-of-key.

songs.title: Las Mañanitas
songs.attribution: Traditional Mexican birthday serenade from the 19th century. The arrangers sometimes credited with fixing its modern form, Manuel M. Ponce (died 1948), Alfonso Esparza Oteo (died 1950) and Alejandro Manzo (died 1950), all died before 1956, so melody and words are public domain. Melody checked against the score in the Wikipedia article (transposed from A to G).

songs.title: O Tannenbaum (O Christmas Tree)

songs.title: O Come, All Ye Faithful
songs.attribution: The tune "Adeste Fideles" is attributed to John Francis Wade, who published it with the Latin hymn in 1751 (he died in 1786); the English words are Frederick Oakeley's translation of 1841 (he died in 1880). Melody and words are public domain worldwide.

Gerdal published in Moscow in 1884; everything was in print well before 1929, so melody and words are public domain. The chromatic notes (D#, G#, A#, C#) belong to the tune and show as out-of-key.

songs.title: Ode to Joy (Joyful, Joyful, We Adore Thee)
songs.attribution: Melody: the "Ode to Joy" theme from Beethoven's Symphony No. 9 (1824); English hymn words "Joyful, joyful, we adore Thee" by Henry van Dyke (1907). Both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Yankee Doodle
songs.attribution: Anglo-American tune and words from the 18th century (the "macaroni" verse was in print by the 1780s); public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Yes Sir, That's My Baby
songs.attribution: Music by Walter Donaldson (died 1947), words by Gus Kahn (died 1941); published by Irving Berlin, Inc. in 1925. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Yigdal
songs.attribution: The Hebrew hymn Yigdal is attributed to Daniel ben Judah of Rome (about 1404). The tune is the old Friday-evening synagogue melody of London's Great Synagogue, made famous by its cantor Myer Lyon ("Leoni", died 1797) and borrowed in 1770 for the English hymn "The God of Abraham Praise"; notation after the Jewish Encyclopedia (1906). First four lines. Both public domain.

songs.title: You Made Me Love You (I Didn't Want to Do It)
songs.attribution: Music by James V. Monaco (died 1945), words by Joseph McCarthy (died 1943); published by Broadway Music Corp. (Will Von Tilzer) in 1913 and introduced by Al Jolson. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: You're a Grand Old Flag
songs.attribution: Words and music by George M. Cohan (died 1942), written for his musical "George Washington, Jr." and published by F. A. Mills, New York, in 1906; this is Cohan's own final wording of the chorus. Public domain: published before 1931 (United States) and all authors died before 1972 (Canada).

songs.title: Its So Cold Without You
songs.attribution: "Its So Cold Without You" by YUKON, from the album "POW-WOW HARD BOOGIE". CC BY 3.0. Published on Jamendo (album 153317); downloaded from the Internet Archive.
